firewallRules.rule: No kernel layer (L0, L1) imports a vertical, project-profile, editor-host, CLI-presentation or compiler-backend owner (L3, L4, LH, LC).
A horizontal product (L2) imports no vertical, project profile, host or compiler backend; it consumes vertical knowledge only as catalog-registered contributions.
A carrier frontend (L3) never imports a compiler backend (LC); a backend may import its own frontend.
Only the composition root (LR) names concrete verticals, project profiles and backends; it registers them statically and publishes one immutable CatalogSnapshot.

A firewall breach that exists at the described head is an equality-pinned exception naming its deletion route (K01, K02); the exception set only shrinks, and it shrinks in the change that lands the route's deletion owner.

outcomes.outcome: Kernel never executes project or framework code: executable ecosystem config is captured outside the kernel, and an unsupported executable config stays uncaptured rather than executed
Every carrier has a frontend; only compile-capable carriers register an optional compiler backend; no compiler is a normal state, never an error path of tooling
Compiler capability is declared per exact vertical release and never inferred from tooling support; compiler/parser conflation is a manifest structural failure

Carrier, semantic-profile and project-profile identities are independent: one carrier byte stream may carry mutually exclusive semantic claims, and a semantic profile activates only on its exact release
A project profile overlays semantic profiles through generic roles, realms and generated facts; it never selects a TypeScript program, owns resolution, mutates an identity, or runs when inapplicable

Public results carry one typed outcome vocabulary (success, partial, ambiguous, NeedInputs, unsupported, not-applicable, cancelled, stale) across Rust, NAPI, WASM, LSP, MCP and CLI; no surface reports empty success for missing inputs
The per-surface capability/maturity matrix is generated from manifests and freshness-checked; no boolean capability lie and no registered no-op handler
Every vertical and horizontal product has its own terminal; no global release join exists, and the superseded release universe (global EXT0/TVG0/PJG0/X1 coupling) has no successor
Soak joins are continuous evidence over accepted terminals: they fix nothing, gate no release, and a failure becomes a non-invalidating follow-up for the exact owner

Extension contributions are data-only or isolated guest execution behind a versioned manifest; they cannot replace core identity, type semantics, resolver, cache validity or edit-transaction authority, and conflict order is deterministic
